## Definition

**Nominal data** consist of categories or names with no inherent order or ranking. Numbers assigned to categories are arbitrary labels, not quantities.

## Characteristics

| Property | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| Categories | Data grouped into distinct classes |
| No order | Categories cannot be ranked |
| No intervals | No meaningful distance between categories |
| Mutually exclusive | Each case belongs to one category |

## Examples

| Variable | Categories |
|----------|------------|
| Gender | Male, Female, Non-binary |
| Eye colour | Brown, Blue, Green, Hazel |
| Blood type | A, B, AB, O |
| Experimental condition | Treatment, Control |
| Country | UK, USA, France, Germany |

## Appropriate Statistics

| Statistic | Use |
|-----------|-----|
| Mode | Most frequent category |
| Frequencies | Count per category |
| Percentages | Proportion per category |
| Chi-square | Test of association |

## Inappropriate Operations

❌ Cannot calculate:

- Mean (what's the "average" of male and female?)
- Median (no order to find middle)
- Standard deviation (no numerical distances)

## Coding Nominal Data

Numbers can be used as labels, but they're arbitrary:

| Gender | Code |
|--------|------|
| Male | 1 |
| Female | 2 |
| Non-binary | 3 |

The numbers don't mean 2 > 1 or that Female > Male.

## Binary/Dichotomous Variables

A special case of nominal with only two categories:

| Variable | Categories |
|----------|------------|
| Correct/Incorrect | 1, 0 |
| Yes/No | 1, 0 |
| Pass/Fail | 1, 0 |

## DataLab Connection

At **Lady Luck**, the choice variable (Safe/Risky) is nominal. At **Reflex Test**, accuracy (Correct/Incorrect) is nominal. Use chi-square tests to analyse relationships between nominal variables.
